The fixtures here are `harness_after_run_history_test.go` (source 694) and `harness_after_run_close_drain_test.go` (source 429 close-in-drain), both known-failing oracles run through the project overlay with the protected prototype replaced only in the compiler input: `go test -overlay <run>/overlay.json ./durable -run '^<function>' -count=1 -timeout=90s` under `$PROJECT_TMP_ROOT/runs/after-run-oracle/20261103/` and `$PROJECT_TMP_ROOT/runs/after-run-close-drain/20261103/` respectively. It fails on the first assertion — the `afterRun` hook is never invoked for a run whose answer follows a model tool round, so the history checks are not reached. The failure is not a selection artifact: it reproduces with the extension selected explicitly on the agent, and with no gate and no compaction, so the tool-round continuation itself skips the hook. The pinned contract (pinned generation.ts864 `answer()` evaluates `asksAfterRun` before the answer commit) requires the hook to run there; native `handoffToolGeneration` carries no afterRun state into the successor checkpoint, and the post-tool answer commit does not evaluate the hook selection. Root cause is narrowed but not fully pinned. The source's ordered kind sequence needs `api.entries(minEntryId..maxEntryId)`; the native `HookAPI` exposes no range scan, so that assertion is not ported, and no API expansion was made.

`harness_after_run_close_drain_test.go` keeps the source429 close-in-drain contract with the source's task shape (attempt recorded, gate-or-abort wait, then commit; abort handler records aborted). Baseline at `e7a17b0`: one failure, 0.101s, on two retained assertions — the abort handler is not run at close (`aborts=0`), and the interrupted attempt is not re-executed (`executions=1`, `commits=1`). Close does not cancel the running drain task; the phase continues past cancellation and its commit lands while the harness closing flag is true, so the task completes at close. If the handler instead surfaces cancellation as an error, native records a decided `faulted` outcome rather than leaving the interrupted attempt pending — the `close_requeue` controls show the requeue path only for handlers that record no outcome. The source expects the interrupted attempt to leave no decided outcome so the reopened harness re-executes it (two attempts, one commit) and the hook stays un-reasked. The source's `test.tests` entry count is not ported (no entry range scan). No runtime change; the close fence must be reconciled before this can pass.

The ended-bridge case (depths 2 and 5) is no longer pending here. Rebuilt in the source's shape through the public transaction surface — `Tx.CreateConversation` for the conversation owned by the deepest link, then a public commit creating the work inside it after that owner ended — it passes in `durable/harness_ownership_ended_bridge_main_test.go`: 2 subtests, 0 fail 0 skip, 0.168s count1, gate of 7 functions 0.884s with vet and gofmt clean. The fixture previously recorded here was an unfaithful reduction that put the work directly under an ended task, which native legitimately rejects (`taskCanOwnNewWork`); that conclusion is withdrawn. The source's own case keeps the work conversation-owned, so native's decided-owner rule is not the contract at issue.

``harness_group_commit_wait_cycle_test.go` keeps source 226 (#11141): two conversation-owned tasks each wait on the other through a memo, admitted behind each other. Measured at `durable/harness_group_commit_main_test.go` sibling run (2026-11-04, count1, 4.243s bounded window): native records no refusal and neither task settles - both committed waiting states point at each other, so the mutual wait deadlocks (refusals empty, ranDone empty). The source asserts the second admitted wait is refused with a wait-cycle error, the first is not refused, and the first completes. Native has no cycle check in the wait-admission path, so this is a divergence needing direction, not a fixture error. Two construction notes: the held-commit capability uses the internal `appendFrame`/`appendFrames` hook because Open rejects a Storage wrapper (session requires native storage), following `TestMainSessionUnpublishedReadBarriers`; and the memo is set with `TaskRuntime.MemoCandidate` inside each task's own commit because native rejects an execution replacement from another commit (execution task replacement requires invocation authority). Recipe: `go test -overlay <run>/overlay.json ./durable -run '^TestPendingGroupCommitRefusesSecondOfTwoOppositeWaits' -count=1 -timeout=45s`.

Future known-failing fixtures belong here only with an explicit project-owned execution recipe, prototype exclusion, retained complete assertions and a concise baseline receipt. Never use a default skip or relaxed expected count to hide a failure.

`harness_group_commit_close_in_flight_test.go` keeps source 758 (#11141): a running invocation, a call admitted and held at Storage, and a close during that call. Measured 2026-11-04 (count1, 0.544s): native close waits for the in-flight call before settling, which matches half the case name, but the running invocation is not signalled during that window - the assertion `close signals the invocation during a call in flight` fails. The retained halves pass unchanged: the held call lands before Storage closes (entry present after reopen) and the reopened invocation is pending again. This is a measured divergence, not a fixture error; it is the same close-fence area as source 429. Recipe: `make test PACKAGES=./durable TEST_FLAGS="-overlay <run>/overlay.json -v -run '^TestPendingGroupCommitCloseSignalsInvocationDuringCallInFlight' -count=1 -timeout=45s"`, with the overlay mapping the protected continuation prototype out of compiler input.

Fixture-capability limits in the same file, recorded without execution (no disposition claimed): cases 491 (scheduler index pins/sweep symbol), 608 and 626 (a mark write and a reconcile pass that must reach the line inside the pending window), 646 (record-cache bound; native has no record cache and no storage-read counter), 699 (submission lookup completing inside the pending window) and 714 (a wait continuation that observes an unpublished group mid-window; native waits are task-scoped `On` + policy, not per-execution). Native admits one writer on the line and no read or write can complete inside the pending window, which `TestMainSessionUnpublishedReadBarriers` already measures; the cases that only assert a reader waits for publication are expressible and pass as `durable/harness_group_commit_main_test.go` `TestMainGroupCommitLineReadsWaitForPendingMembership` (cases 363, 404, 446).

`session_group_commit_refusal_test.go` keeps source 414 (row 337, refusal half): a batch the storage refuses must fail the Session, so every outcome after it reports `SessionFailed` and the session end carries the refusal. Measured 2026-11-04 (count1, 1.092s, reproduces unchanged at 1.072s after the gates controls were added): native reports the refusal as `StorageRejected` - no write was admitted - does not latch the Session, and the operation admitted after it succeeds. The fence native does implement is measured as a passing control in `durable/session_group_commit_main_test.go` (`TestMainSessionFailureFenceKeepsEarlierPartsAfterSettlementError`): an error during settlement latches the Session, a later read reports `SessionFailed`, `Closed` reports `failed`, and the earlier part stays durable while the failed part never lands. Native's reported cause is its own classification ("uncertain storage outcome"), not the storage error the source expects, so that assertion is not met. Two limits recorded without resolution: native has no predicate-based backend refusal inside a call, so the nearest expressible refusal is the storage's own admission refusal; and the source's three parts admitted while the first call is in flight cannot be reproduced because native admits one writer on the line. Recipe: `make test PACKAGES=./durable TEST_FLAGS="-overlay <run>/overlay.json -v -run '^TestPendingGroupCommitRefusalFailsTheSession' -count=1 -timeout=45s"`.

## Conversation-view document identity (v1.5.0 source330)

`harness_view_shared_docs_test.go` retains `harness-view.test.ts:330`'s assertion that simultaneous observers share the same `docs` object. Native `ConversationWatch.Value()` deep-copies its result: equal contents have different live map identities. The fixture records that failure and continues through the listener-isolation assertions, which pass. Initial failure 0.058s; count3 after adding the content-equality precondition: three expected failures, 0.074s. This measures the public accessor contract; internal mount sharing is unverified. Native's detached-copy ownership control also passes, so an identity fix needs contract reconciliation. See `docs/upstream-v1.5.0/view-shared-identity.md`.

Use a directory beneath the resolved project run root. Create `prototype_stub.go` containing `package durable` and an `overlay.json` with these replacements (absolute paths):

```json
{
  "Replace": {
    "/workspace/projects/go-ai/durable/continuation_prototype_main_test.go": "<run>/prototype_stub.go",
    "/workspace/projects/go-ai/durable/zz_pending_view_identity_test.go": "/workspace/projects/go-ai/durable/testdata/upstream-main/pending/harness_view_shared_docs_test.go"
  }
}
```

Run `make test PACKAGES=./durable TEST_FLAGS="-overlay <run>/overlay.json -v -run TestPendingViewObserversShareDocsIdentity -count=1 -timeout=30s"`. The prototype itself is unchanged. Dispose of the run directory after analysis.

The same view-identity overlay also compiles:

- `TestPendingViewSource160UnchangedMapIdentity`: exact touching-frame count/configuration delta and unchanged contents pass; unchanged `pi.live` and `docs` map identities fail. The source's initial empty entries-array object identity is unexecuted because Go slice pointers cannot establish it.
- `TestPendingViewSource525WindowDocsIdentity`: windows `{min:2,max:3}` and `{min:5}` over six notes plus one append have equal document contents but different document maps. The independent content/window assertions pass as `TestMainViewSource525IndependentWindowContents`.

Run `-run 'TestPendingViewSource(160|525)'` with that overlay. At parent `c422344`, count3/shuffle42 gives six expected failures in 0.258s; five focused passing functions give 15 passes in 1.975s. Source160 initialises configuration before recording to match `openChat(chatSetup())`; the bare-fixture normalisation probe is uncredited. Runtime ownership is unchanged.

## Session group admission and batching (v1.5.0 source170)

`session_group_commit_batching_test.go` retains the source's held-first-call assertion: independent callbacks b/c both execute before a's storage call is released; no publication occurs before release; calls contain `[1, 2]` parts; outcomes settle a/b/c; publication sequences are three distinct increasing values. It creates three separate conversation-scoped note addresses and uses native `appendFrame`/`appendFrames` hooks and the private standalone stored-observer lane. Go goroutine completion order is an adaptation of JS promise settlement order, not a proof of JS microtask/macrotask ordering. `Done()`-evaluation witnesses show b/c attempted Session admission; cleanup releases storage and joins workers before closing.

At parent `6f53cc6`, count3/shuffle42: three expected failures in 3.210s. Each run reports b/c did not execute during the held call and native call sizes `[1,1,1]`, rather than `[1,2]`. No premature publication, completion-order or distinct-increasing-sequence assertion failed in those runs. Six related controls pass count1 in 2.364s; vet with the pending oracle compiled and formatting/diff checks pass. This is not a concurrency or whole-file parity pass.

Use the project-root overlay recipe above, mapping virtual `zz_packet_pending_test.go` to this file (instead of the view fixture) and excluding the protected prototype. Run `make test PACKAGES=./durable TEST_FLAGS="-overlay <run>/overlay.json -v -run TestPendingSessionGroupCommitBatchesAdmittedParts -count=1 -timeout=30s"`. Remove run data after analysis.
